newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra says to cut states A$139 million.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra says to cut states A$139 million.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Friday the cut in federal funding to the states would not exceed A$139 million next fiscal year, not the A$410 million asserted by the states earlier.

Costello and Prime Minister John Howard also said the refusal of the states to accept the offer at Friday's Premiers Conference was meaningless, because the cut in special-purpose grants was something for the Canberra alone to decide.
"That is not a negotiated figure," Howard told reporters.
The federal government was standing by its commitment to the general grants, which were negotiable, he added.
Costello said his figure of A$139 million was the variation from the figure already in forward estimates for next fiscal year, to June 1998.
Further, that was only a maximum variation, he said. The actual change announced in the May budget might be less.
It was unclear how the states had calculated their figure of A$410 million, although they described it as the loss of grants in real terms -- that is, after inflation.
The states do not levy their own income tax and depend on federal government money called general-purpose grants to sustain their budgets.
The federal government also pays the states additional money as specific-purpose grants, which the states have to spend as Canberra directs -- for example, on hospitals.
Last year the states agreed to temporarily sacrifice some of their general-purpose grants to help the federal government with its budget problems.

Costello said that money would remain as previously budgeted. But the specific-purpose grants, which Canberra sees as money directed to its own policy priorities, were cut last year and would be cut again this year by the A$139 million.

The states see the specific-purpose grants as relieving pressure on their own spending. If Canberra reduced a state's funding for roads, for example, the state might feel itself forced to find more road money from other sources.
The federal government last year cut its own budget by A$7 billion (1997/98 full-year) and says it needs to find another A$2 billion a year to bring the 1998/99 budget into balance.
